components.css: .ds-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 10px; min-height: 50px; padding: 0 23px; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 999px; font-family: 'Manrope Variable', Manrope, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.9rem; font-weight: 720; letter-spacing: -0.012em; line-height: 1; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 200ms cubic-bezier(0.23,1,0.32,1), border-color 200ms cubic-bezier(0.23,1,0.32,1), transform 200ms cubic-bezier(0.23,1,0.32,1), box-shadow 200ms cubic-bezier(0.23,1,0.32,1); } .ds-btn svg { transition: transform 200ms cubic-bezier(0.23,1,0.32,1); } .ds-btn-primary { background: #2b46d6; color: #f6f5f1; box-shadow: 0 18px 40px -22px rgba(23,25,31,0.4), inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.28); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #3b5bff; transform: translateY(-2px); box-shadow: 0 24px 46px -22px rgba(23,25,31,0.5), inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.35); } .ds-btn:hover svg { transform: translate(2px,-2px); } .ds-btn:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #2b46d6; outline-offset: 4px; } .ds-btn:active { transform: scale(0.97); transition-duration: 120ms; }

narrative.overview:
Omnitron looks like a well-run operations room at nine in the morning: bright, quiet and exact. Corporate tech that feels made in 2030, not a neon command deck. The ground is Warm Bone, the instruments are Omnitron Blue, and the heavy panels are Deep Ops Navy. Every screen implies someone is at the controls. Workflows end in a human decision, and the interface reads as instrumentation for that person, not as a machine running on its own.

The system is full-bleed and band-based. Each section is a plate that runs edge to edge, separated by color blocking rather than boxes: light ground, navy statement band, near-white reading section, navy again, then the one saturated Omnitron Blue call to action, closing on footer navy. A fine blueprint grid with soft light pools sits behind every plate, so even empty areas look instrumented rather than blank. Components are tactile and engineered. Pill controls lift slightly on hover and press in. Cards carry layered, navy-tinted shadows with a top-edge highlight, like machined parts under daylight.

Visuals are literal and crisp. Processes are drawn as flow diagrams, numbered steppers and labelled nodes. 3D is welcome but rendered sharply (orthographic, no bloom or fog), never as soft abstract shapes. Copy stays short so the diagrams carry the explanation.
keyCharacteristics: Full-bleed bands with deliberate tone blocking (bone → navy → paper → navy → blue CTA → footer navy).
A blueprint grid with light pools behind every section; dead space is textured, never blank.
One accent: Omnitron Blue. No orange or other warm accent.
A confident grotesque display (Archivo) with tight tracking, calm Manrope body text and JetBrains Mono uppercase labels.
Tactile pills, hairline structure, navy-tinted layered elevation.
Literal, crisp diagrams: numbered steps, flow lines with dots, the result step in blue.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Omnitron Blue is the only accent. Orange and other warm accents are retired. Never add a second hue for emphasis; use weight, size or the navy tone instead.

rules.name: The Tone Scope Rule
rules.body: A section never hard-codes colours. It picks a tone (`default`, `--paper`, `.tone-navy`, `.tone-blue`, footer) and every token inside it is re-scoped. Light cards may sit inside navy bands via `.tone-light`.

rules.name: The One Blue Block Rule
rules.body: Only the closing CTA band uses Omnitron Blue as a background. Every other band alternates between light and navy.

rules.name: The Tight Grotesque Rule
rules.body: Archivo headings track tight (-0.01em to -0.038em) and use balanced wrapping. Don't loosen tracking toward 0, and don't swap in a serif or a playful geometric display face.

rules.name: The Mono Means Metadata Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono is for labels, indexes and technical meta only, always uppercase and tracked. Never set sentences or body copy in mono.

rules.name: The Tinted Shadow Rule
rules.body: Every shadow is tinted navy or blue. A neutral grey `rgba(0,0,0,…)` drop shadow on a light surface is off-system.

rules.name: The Crisp Depth Rule
rules.body: Depth comes from layered shadows, tone and parallax, never from blur. No bloom, fog or soft-focus 3D; scenes stay sharp and literal.

dos: **Do** pick a tone class for every new section and keep the light / navy alternation. Omnitron Blue as a background belongs to the closing CTA only.
**Do** fill wide gaps with the blueprint-grid backdrop or a larger visual instead of leaving blank gutters.
**Do** draw processes literally: numbered steps, flow lines with dots, labelled nodes, and the final step in blue.
**Do** tint every shadow navy or blue and add the top-edge highlight to raised surfaces.
**Do** keep hover motion behind `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` and UI feedback under 300ms (press 120ms, UI 200ms, panels 280ms), with strong ease-out curves.
**Do** give every 3D or scroll scene a static fallback for small screens and reduced motion.
donts: **Don't** reintroduce orange or any second accent hue.
**Don't** render concepts as abstract, blurry 3D (bloom, fog, soft blobs). Keep 3D orthographic and crisp.
**Don't** use a serif or playful geometric display face, or loosen Archivo's tight tracking.
**Don't** set body copy in JetBrains Mono, or use pure black text or neutral grey shadows.
**Don't** box sections in bordered containers. Bands are full-bleed and structure comes from hairlines.
**Don't** copy the dark terminal palette of the current omnitron.tech. Borrow its structure (steppers, dotted grids, 01/03 numbered pagination), not its colours.
